answer: In a Wesolowski VDF, each identity must answer a fresh challenge by performing a chain of dependent modular squarings; the next step cannot begin before the previous one finishes, limiting speedups for that proof across GPUs. An attacker may run separate chains for clones in parallel, so the delay is not absolute Sybil resistance: it imposes a per-identity time and hardware cost, even when onyx, gale, and saffron are among the challenge labels.
